title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Tellurium (Te, Z=52) is 127.60(3)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Tellurium (Te, Z=52) as 127.60(3), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 52, symbol Te, as Tellurium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Tellurium as 127.60(3). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Isotope rows in the same file: Te-120 relative atomic mass 119.9040593(33), isotopic composition 0.0009(1); Te-122 relative atomic mass 121.9030435(16), isotopic composition 0.0255(12); Te-123 relative atomic mass 122.9042698(16), isotopic composition 0.0089(3); Te-124 relative atomic mass 123.9028171(16), isotopic composition 0.0474(14); Te-125 relative atomic mass 124.9044299(16), isotopic composition 0.0707(15); Te-126 relative atomic mass 125.9033109(16), isotopic composition 0.1884(25); Te-128 relative atomic mass 127.90446128(93), isotopic composition 0.3174(8); Te-130 relative atomic mass 129.906222748(12), isotopic composition 0.3408(62). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
